featured_reviews.name: Sachin Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently tried the much-hyped batata vada at Shree Krishna Batata Wada in Dadar, and honestly, I was left disappointed. The taste was quite ordinary — nothing extraordinary or unique about it. I had high expectations given the name and long-standing reputation, but the flavor didn’t stand out at all. To top it off, the pricing was shockingly high — ₹27 for just one single vada (not even a plate!). For a simple street snack that’s supposed to be pocket-friendly and satisfying, this felt like a complete rip-off.

There was no chutney or accompaniment that enhanced the taste, and the vada itself lacked spice and crunch. It felt like they were cashing in purely on the legacy or nostalgia rather than actual quality or taste. In a city like Mumbai, where you get amazing batata vadas at countless local joints, this place didn’t meet expectations at all.

If you're a true batata vada lover, I’d suggest exploring other options around Dadar or even in nearby areas — there are definitely better places in terms of both taste and value for money. My honest opinion — a BIG NO to this place. Not worth the hype or the price.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Muni
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Surti Farsan Mart is one of those places that every foodie in Mumbai has strong opinions about, and after trying them, I can finally see why. I stopped by recently to grab a quick snack, and here is my honest take on the experience.

The Food (The Star of the Show):
Let's get straight to the point—their samosa is exceptional. The outer shell is perfectly crisp and flaky, not too thick, and shatters beautifully when you bite into it. The filling inside is well-spiced and flavorful without being too greasy. But what truly elevates the entire experience is their chutney. It is an absolute game-changer. It strikes that perfect balance between sweet, tangy, and spicy, complementing the samosa so well that you will find yourself asking for extra portions. If you are a samosa connoisseur, this is a must-try.

The Vibe & Service:
Being a farsan mart, it operates with that classic "counter-service" efficiency. It can get quite crowded, especially during evening snack time, so be prepared to wait a few minutes to place your order. The staff is efficient, though they are clearly accustomed to the rush.

The Price Factor:
Now, onto the one point that keeps this from being a perfect 5-star review for me: the pricing. There is no denying that the quality is top-tier, but the cost is undeniably on the higher side compared to your average local snack joint. You are paying a premium for the brand name and the location. While the taste justifies the splurge occasionally, it is the kind of place you go to when you want a "treat yourself" snack rather than an everyday cheap eat.

Verdict:
If you love samosas and want to taste one of the best versions available in Mumbai, you have to visit Dadar Surti Farsan Mart. Just go in knowing that your wallet will feel a slightly lighter for the experience

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
On a rainy Sunday, I visited Dadar Surti Farsan, a well-known spot for traditional Gujarati snacks, and the experience was absolutely delightful. The drizzle outside made it the perfect day to indulge in some hot and savory farsan, and this place did not disappoint. The shop has a simple, no-fuss vibe, but what truly stands out is the freshness and authenticity of the food served.

I began with their **soft and spongy dhokla**, which was perfectly steamed, light on the stomach, and mildly tangy with just the right hint of sweetness. Topped with mustard seeds and curry leaves, it had that authentic Gujarati touch. Next, I tried the makai roll, which was both unique and flavorful. The subtle sweetness of corn paired with the spices made it a wholesome snack and something I’d definitely go back for.

The highlight for me, however, was the pyaz kachori. Crispy on the outside and generously stuffed with a spicy onion mixture inside, it was comfort food at its best—especially when enjoyed hot on a rainy day. Each bite was bursting with flavor and paired perfectly with the chutneys served alongside.

One of the best parts about Dadar Surti Farsan is its **reasonable pricing**. Despite the quality and freshness of the items, the rates are pocket-friendly, making it a great place for both quick bites and takeaway parcels. The staff was quick and efficient, ensuring customers didn’t have to wait long even though the place was quite busy.

Overall, my visit to Dadar Surti Farsan was an enjoyable mix of great taste, tradition, and value for money. For anyone who enjoys authentic Gujarati snacks, this place is a must-try and the experience becomes even more special when savored on a rainy day.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.
featured_reviews.review_text:
A friend recommended this Irani cafe, so I visited with my family, and it turned out to be a wonderful experience. We ordered kheema pav, bheja fry, and chicken cutlets  and every dish was absolutely delicious. The mutton kheema was full of rich flavors, so well cooked that we didn’t even need the usual onion and lemon on the side. The bheja fry was equally tasty, perfectly spiced and authentic.
The chicken cutlets deserve a special mention  crispy, juicy, and simply irresistible. My son loved them so much, which made the meal even more enjoyable for us.
We ended our meal with classic bun maska pav and Irani tea pure comfort and nostalgia. Words really fall short to describe how good it was.
The ambience truly adds to the charm of the place. It has a traditional Irani cafe design slightly old fashioned yet classic, giving a warm, nostalgic vibe that makes you feel connected to the heritage.
One more lovely thing about this place is the owner  extremely kind, polite, and well spoken, which adds a very personal and welcoming touch to the overall experience. I even clicked a photo to keep the memory of this visit.
Just a small thing to note , the cafe accepts cash only, so it’s better to carry cash as digital payments like GPay aren’t available.
Overall, an excellent place for authentic Irani cafe food with great hospitality. Highly recommended, and I would definitely love to visit again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
On a rainy Sunday, I had the pleasure of visiting **Café Colony**, a charming Irani café located in Hindu Colony, Dadar. The weather itself was perfect for the experience, as the comforting aroma of freshly brewed tea and baked bread created a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. The café has that classic Irani charm, with its simple yet inviting interiors that make you feel at home the moment you step in.

I began with their famous **Irani chai and brun maska**, and it was everything I had hoped for. The chai was strong, perfectly balanced with milk and sugar, and paired beautifully with the soft-yet-crispy brun generously slathered with butter. It was the kind of combination that instantly lifts your mood on a rainy day. Next, I tried the **keema fry with pav**, which turned out to be another highlight of the visit. The keema was spiced just right—rich, hearty, and bursting with authentic flavor—while the pav was fresh and fluffy, making it a wholesome and satisfying dish.

To end the meal on a sweet note, I indulged in their famous **gaz sweet**, a delicacy that lived up to its reputation. Its unique taste and texture added a perfect finishing touch to the experience, leaving me with a lasting impression of the café’s culinary heritage.

What made the visit even more special was the interaction with the lady owner of Café Colony. She was warm, courteous, and genuinely interested in knowing how we enjoyed the food. During our conversation, I shared that I am from Delhi and thoroughly enjoyed experiencing these authentic Irani dishes in Mumbai. Her hospitality, combined with the food, made the outing truly memorable.

Overall, Café Colony is not just about food—it’s about warmth, tradition, and conversations. A must-visit gem in Dadar.

In mains, the Chicken Bhuna with Tandoor Roti was a comforting combination and absolutely delicious. Ended the meal with a Caramel Pudding, which was the perfect sweet note to finish on.

featured_reviews.name: omkar bugade
featured_reviews.review_text:
The service and atmosphere here are really nice, and the location is incredibly easy to find. They clearly use high-quality ingredients,
but when it comes to the actual flavor, they really need to work on it.

**For a total bill of around ₹440, the meal just wasn't worth it.**

​Here is how the food fared:

​Rasa Shiravale (4/10): Very average, lacked depth.
​Kalya Vatanyachi Usal (8/10): Tasty and well-made.
​Vade (7/10): Good flavor, but they were quite small and on the oilier side.
​Batatyachi Kapa (4/10): A massive disappointment. Kapa is usually foolproof, but these were thin, soggy, and soft instead of crispy. Plus, there was an overpowering taste of raw ginger-garlic paste.
​Sol Kadhi (8/10): Refreshing and good.

​Final Verdict: Great hospitality and potential, but the kitchen definitely needs to fine-tune its execution to justify the pricing.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much for taking the time to share such detailed feedback. We truly appreciate your kind words about our service, atmosphere, and ingredients — it means a lot to us.

We’re also grateful for your honest feedback regarding the food. As a newly started kitchen, we are continuously learning, refining, and working hard to improve consistency and flavours every single day. Your observations about the Rasa Shiravale, Batatyachi Kapa, and Vade have been noted carefully and shared with our kitchen team for improvement.

Regarding the flavours, some of our dishes are prepared in a traditional Konkan style, where the seasoning is intentionally more subtle and balanced compared to heavily spiced restaurant-style preparations. Rasa Shiravale, for example, is meant to have a light and comforting flavour profile that highlights coconut rather than very bold sweet taste. Similarly, Batatyachi Kapa and Vade are traditionally served as simpler accompaniments to balance the overall meal.

That said, we completely understand that taste preferences can differ, and we genuinely value your perspective. We are continuously working on improving execution, texture, and consistency while staying true to authentic Konkan flavours.

We’re happy to know you enjoyed the Kalya Vatanyachi Usal and Sol Kadhi, and we truly hope you’ll visit us again to experience the improvements we’re working towards.

Mamaji Taste of Katta in Matunga offers a delightful experience, and their chocolate sandwich is a must-try. Upon entering..... The sandwich is generously filled with rich, creamy chocolate that melts in your mouth with each bite. Mamaji’s Frankies are overall great — the taste and quality are really good. However, there’s room for improvement in a couple of items:

1. Manchurian Frankie: The Manchurian pieces were quite oily, making each bite feel heavy. Reducing the oil content would really enhance the taste.

2. Tandoori Paneer Frankie: This one was disappointing — it felt more like a regular paneer frankie with a ready-made tandoori sauce. When you call it tandoori, we expect that authentic, flavorful tandoori masala touch.

Hope they take this feedback positively — the rest of their menu is definitely worth trying!

Mamaji Taste of Katta in Matunga offers a delightful culinary experience, and their chocolate sandwich is a must-try. Upon entering, the cozy, welcoming atmosphere immediately sets the tone for a pleasant meal. The menu boasts an array of delectable treats, but the chocolate sandwich stands out.

The sandwich is generously filled with rich, creamy chocolate that melts in your mouth with each bite. The bread is perfectly toasted, providing a satisfying crunch that complements the smoothness of the chocolate. It's clear that quality ingredients are used, making each element of the sandwich taste fresh and flavorful. The balance of sweetness is just right—not too overpowering, yet indulgent enough to satisfy any chocolate lover's cravings.

Service at Mamaji Taste of Katta is efficient and friendly, adding to the overall enjoyable dining experience. The staff is attentive and ensures that orders are served promptly. The ambiance, combined with the excellent food, makes it a perfect spot for a quick snack or a relaxed meal.

In conclusion, Mamaji Taste of Katta’s chocolate sandwich is a delicious treat that shouldn't be missed. Whether you're a local or just passing through Matunga, this spot is worth a visit for its mouthwatering offerings.
